heroHeadline: Day 960: 38 Days to Supreme Court July 1 Accountability Deadline — Knesset Kallner Inquiry Bill Advancing Toward First Plenum Reading; WSJ Reveals Israel's Secret NILI Task Force Has Compiled Full List of All ~3,000 October 7 Participants; Hundreds Killed or Arrested Through Ceasefire
heroSubtitle: The deadliest attack on Jewish people since the Holocaust — assault timeline, hostage crisis resolved January 2026, intelligence failures, and IDF response. May 24, 2026 (Day 960 / Ceasefire Day 227): Two major October 7 accountability developments emerged this week. On May 21–22 (Day 958), the Wall Street Journal revealed Israel's secret NILI task force — a Shin Bet + military intelligence unit that compiled a comprehensive database of all ~3,000 October 7 participants and has been systematically killing or arresting each one; 'hundreds' have been crossed off the list. On May 22 (Day 958), Al Jazeera published an in-depth analysis raising international concerns about Israel's Knesset-passed (93–0, May 12) military tribunal for ~300 detained October 7 participants — specifically that it may use secret evidence, allow absent-defendant hearings, and mandate public broadcasting of proceedings while applying the death penalty to Palestinians but not Israeli citizens convicted of killing Palestinians. On May 23 (Day 959): France banned National Security Minister Itamar Ben Gvir from French territory over his 'unspeakable' actions taunting Gaza flotilla detainees; bereaved families renewed accountability demands — Maayan Sherman: 'Refusal to form a commission spits on Ron's grave.' As of May 24 (Day 960), 38 days remain until the Supreme Court's July 1 deadline for a credible October 7 investigation. The Kallner inquiry bill (which dropped 'independent investigation' language, bars judges) advances toward a first Knesset plenum reading expected in late May. The opposition Beyachad alliance (Bennett-Lapid) pledges an independent state commission as Day 1 of any new government. NILI campaign continues through ceasefire; Phase Two deadlock persists (Hamas disarmament deadlines all expired); IDF documents 19 ceasefire violations May 6–20 including weapons production; Board of Peace presented six-month report to UNSC May 21 calling Hamas 'principal obstacle' to Phase Two. All 251 hostages accounted for as of January 26, 2026.
